title: Matplotlib + Seaborn Python Tutorial: 5 Charts Every Data Scientist Needs
description:
Your charts get judged before your model does — and nobody warns you about this. In this tutorial, you'll learn why matplotlib and seaborn are not competing libraries and how to use them together to build professional visualizations that actually communicate your analysis.

This is Tutorial 5 of 10 in the Python for Data Science series. By the end, you'll have a setup block that makes every notebook chart look professional, five essential plot types with full code, a multi-panel dashboard, and the save settings that prevent blurry slides.

We use the classic Titanic dataset throughout — it ships with seaborn, no download needed.

[TIMESTAMPS_PLACEHOLDER]

What you'll build:
• A one-block style baseline that every chart inherits automatically
• Distribution, relationship, categorical, correlation, and grouped distribution charts
• A 2×2 dashboard figure in under 25 lines of code
• PNG and vector output saved at publication quality

The shift this tutorial is really about: from 'how do I make this chart' to 'what does this chart need to say.'

[LINKS_PLACEHOLDER]

Tutorial 6 covers statistical testing with scipy and statsmodels — how to tell if what you see in the charts is actually real.
